what: Why splines, and why they are awkward here
title: Restricted cubic splines for complex survey data
text: Real exposure–outcome relationships rarely straight lines. usual workarounds cost something: categorising continuous exposure throws away information power, assuming linearity misspecifies model, polynomials behave badly extremes. Restricted cubic splines fit smooth curve constrained linear beyond outer knots, keeps tails stable leaving middle flexible. Complex surveys NHANES make awkward. Valid analysis needs three design features: sampling weights, without point estimates biased population, clustering stratification, without standard errors — therefore every confidence interval p-value — wrong. rms, natural home restricted cubic splines R, know . survey handles three spline helper. svyrcs bridge: spline fitted inside survey model, estimates use weights confidence band uses Taylor linearisation design degrees freedom.
code: library(svyrcs) library(survey) library(survival)

title: Restricted cubic splines for complex survey data
text: spline curve defined reference: every estimate contrast exposure value. svyrcs supports choices seen literature, choice purely presentational — shifts curve without changing shape either p-value. "median" (default) survey-weighted population median — median unweighted sample, property happened sampled. "min" anchors minimum-risk point, whole curve reads “excess risk relative healthiest value”. common choice obesity literature. "max", "mean", "quantile" (ref_prob), number like also accepted.
code: fits <- lapply(   c("median", "min", "max"),   function(r) svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex,                      design = design, ref = r) ) vapply(fits, function(f) f$ref$value, numeric(1)) #> [1] 27.3500 27.1304 17.8500 plot(fits[[2]], xlab = "Body mass index (kg/m²)", title = TRUE)

what: Does the curve differ by subgroup?
title: Restricted cubic splines for complex survey data
text: Cross spline grouping variable svyrcs() fits one model, returning curve per group:  Two questions get separate answers. Interaction asks whether association differs groups . Shape interaction drops linear interaction term, asks narrower question: curvature differ, one curve simply shifted copy ? neither close significant, worth dwelling . two curves figure look different — minimum sits couple BMI units higher women, male curve climbs sooner — 31 design degrees freedom separation well inside noise. Reporting “association stronger men” fit supported. Subgroup curves easy -read, exactly interaction p-value printed next . facet = TRUE gives group panel bands overlap much read:  details worth knowing: One model, several. Covariate effects — age — shared across groups. Fitting subgroup separately estimate independently produce interaction test . groups share one reference value, curves comparable. ref = "min" reference minimum-risk point reference level, output names . standard error non-reference group accounts covariance main interaction coefficients. Adding two variances separately, obvious shortcut, gives wrong interval. modifier must factor, character logical. Continuous effect modification supported. predict(fit, x = ..., group = "Female") gives numbers one group.

Knots reference fixed model fitted, average survey-weighted quantiles across imputations. convenience: imputation chose knots, five coefficient vectors estimates five different parameterisations Rubin’s rules apply . degrees freedom mitools’. MIcombine() reports (m-1)(1+1/r)^2, upper bound — design, 31 degrees freedom, returns numbers thousands sometimes Inf. Feeding t quantile give confidence intervals far narrow, error using normal quantile worse. svyrcs applies Barnard-Rubin correction, bounded complete-data degrees freedom: df column sits 31 drops fraction missing information (fmi) highest. nothing model imputed, fmi zero, df exactly 31, result identical complete-data fit. joint tests treated way. denominator degrees freedom adjusted rather taken usual multiple-imputation rule, derived imputation structure alone ignores survey design.
code: library(mice) library(mitools)  vars <- c("age", "sex", "race", "bmi", "tchol", "hdl", "time", "event") imp <- mice(nhanes_bmi[vars], m = 5, method = "pmm", maxit = 3, printFlag = FALSE, seed = 1)  completed <- lapply(1:5, function(i) {   cbind(complete(imp, i), nhanes_bmi[c("psu", "strata", "weight")]) })  mi_design <- svydesign(   id = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~weight,   nest = TRUE, data = imputationList(completed) )  fit_mi <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex + tchol, design = mi_design) fit_mi #> Restricted cubic spline on a complex survey design #>  #>   Model      survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards #>   Outcome    Surv(time, event) #>   Exposure   bmi, 4 knots at 19.78, 25.22, 29.71, 40.67 (weighted quantiles) #>   Sample     10,617 observations, 1,893 events, 31 design df #>   Reference  bmi = 27.35 (weighted median), HR = 1 #>   Imputed    m = 5, fraction of missing information 7.4e-05 to 0.00097 (median 0.00045) #>              degrees of freedom reduced from 31 by Barnard-Rubin #>  #>   Overall association  F = 45.93 on 3 and 29.2 df,  p = 3.61e-11  #>   Non-linearity        F = 53.27 on 2 and 29.2 df,  p = 1.83e-10 head(predict(fit_mi, x = c(18, 22, 27, 35, 45))) #>    x estimate  conf.low conf.high          se       df          fmi #> 1 18 2.751244 2.0973163  3.609062 0.132728379 29.16176 0.0005025178 #> 2 22 1.480123 1.3248047  1.653651 0.054217717 29.16678 0.0003313869 #> 3 27 1.000361 0.9914646  1.009338 0.004369014 29.17236 0.0001405740 #> 4 35 1.229373 1.0900634  1.386487 0.058818934 29.16485 0.0003971519 #> 5 45 1.736036 1.4969291  2.013335 0.072471578 29.14803 0.0009679880

code: library(svyrcs) library(survey) library(survival)  design <- svydesign(   id = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~weight,   nest = TRUE, data = nhanes_bmi )  fit <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex + race, design = design) fit #> Restricted cubic spline on a complex survey design #> #>   Model      survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards #>   Outcome    Surv(time, event) #>   Exposure   bmi, 4 knots at 19.78, 25.22, 29.71, 40.67 (weighted quantiles) #>   Sample     10,617 observations, 1,893 events, 31 design df #>   Reference  bmi = 27.35 (weighted median), HR = 1 #> #>   Overall association  F = 43.58 on 3 and 31 df,  p = 3.12e-11 #>   Non-linearity        F = 51.70 on 2 and 31 df,  p = 1.34e-10  plot(fit)                          # curve with confidence band (ggplot2 if installed) summary(fit)                       # turning points, where the band excludes the null predict(fit, x = c(25, 30, 35))    # estimates at values you choose svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age, design = design, ref = "min") by_sex <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) * sex + age, design = design) by_sex$tests$interaction   # p for interaction by_sex$tests$shape         # does the *curvature* differ, or is the curve just shifted? plot(by_sex)               # one coloured curve per group; facet = TRUE to panel them design_mi <- svydesign(id = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~weight,                        nest = TRUE, data = mitools::imputationList(completed_datasets)) svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + tchol, design = design_mi)

survival outcome: all-cause mortality, anchored at the minimum-risk BMI # \donttest{ library(survival) fit_hr <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex,                  design = design, ref = "min") summary(fit_hr) #> Restricted cubic spline on a complex survey design #>  #>   Model      survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards #>   Outcome    Surv(time, event) #>   Exposure   bmi, 4 knots at 19.78, 25.22, 29.71, 40.67 (weighted quantiles) #>   Sample     10,617 observations, 1,893 events, 31 design df #>   Reference  bmi = 27.13 (minimum-risk point), HR = 1 #>  #>   Overall association  F = 48.07 on 3 and 31 df,  p = 9.1e-12  #>   Non-linearity        F = 56.15 on 2 and 31 df,  p = 4.95e-11  #>  #>   Curve shape #>     Lowest    bmi = 27.13,  HR = 1.00 (1.00, 1.00) #>     Highest   bmi = 17.85,  HR = 2.85 (2.17, 3.75) #>     95% band excludes HR = 1 over: #>       bmi 17.85 to 25.40  (HR > 1) #>       bmi 31.06 to 49.14  (HR > 1) plot(fit_hr)   # binary outcome: odds of high total cholesterol fit_or <- svyrcs(high_chol ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex, design = design,                  family = quasibinomial())  # one curve per subgroup, with a test of whether they differ fit_by_sex <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) * sex + age, design = design) fit_by_sex$tests$interaction$p_F #> [1] 0.4796278 plot(fit_by_sex)  #
